sentences.text: ...Respondents CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HARKESH MANUJA
Present: Mr. Sanjiv Gupta, Sr. Advocate, assisted by  Mr. Anuj Gupta, Advocate for the petitioner(s).
Ms. Komal Sharma, DAG, Haryana.
Mr. H.S. Gill, Advocate (through VC) for HSVP.

* * **
HARKESH MANUJA, J. (ORAL)

This order shall dispose off a batch of the present 20 revision pe- titions, bearing CR Nos. 8091,
7997, 8526, 8425, 7701, 7641, 6682, 7871, 7881, 8102, 7651, 7676, 7665, 8174, 7635, 7929, 7990,
7992 and 8545-2025, RFA-1013 & 783-2025 as the common question of law and facts are involved in these petitions.
For the sake of convenience, facts are being culled out from CR No. 7621 of 2025.

[2] By way of revision petition bearing CR No. 7621 of 2025 filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, challenge has been laid to an order dated 07.07.2025 (Annexure P-4) vide which the execution filed by the petitioner has been dismissed as fully satisfied, without taking into considera- 1 of 4 CR No. 7621 of 2025 (O&M) and "21" connected cases 2 tion the full amount tendered and for further direction for execution of the complete award.

FACTS [3] Briefly, the facts are that in pursuance of Haryana Govt. Notification under Section 4 of Himani Alias Himani Grewal Toor vs State Of Haryana And Others on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118620454/
1 the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "1894 Act") issued on 19.12.2002, certain land of the petitioner-landowner situated within the revenue estate of Village Khairpur, Tehsil and District Sirsa was acquired.

entities.text: Himani Alias Himani Grewal Toor vs State Of Haryana And Others on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The acquisition was made for public purpose, namely, for "development of residential and commercial Sectors 19 and 20 at Sirsa.

After completing the requisite formalities under Section 6 of the 1894 Act, an Award No. 11 dated 16.12.2005 came to be passed by the Land Acquisition Collector, HUDA, Hisar (for short "LAC"), whereby the market value of the acquired land was assessed at the rate of Rs. 6 lakhs per acre besides other statutory benefits as permissible under the 1894 Act.

[4] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the 1894 Act, which were ac- cepted vide decision dated 02.05.2011 by the learned Reference Court, whereby market value of the acquired land was assessed / enhanced at the rate of Rs. 525/- per square yard alongwith other statutory benefits.

[5] Still aggrieved, the petitioner approached this Court having preferred RFA No. 7245 of 2011, which was decided on 02.09.2015, further enhancing the market value from Rs. 525/- per square yard to Rs. 612/- per square yard with other statutory benefits.
2 of 4 CR No. 7621 of 2025 (O&M) and "21" connected cases 3

[6] Challenging the adjudication made by this Court, the petitioner- landowner approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court by filing SLP No(s). 36087-36124 of 2015, tilted "Piyara Singh and anr. Versus State of Haryana and others",
seeking further enhancement of the market value.

entities.text: Piyara Singh and anr. Versus State of Haryana and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A bunch of appeals/SLPs were disposed off by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 17.11.2016 (Annexure P-1) and the market value was enhanced to Rs. 1,020/- per square yard with other statutory benefits.
[7] On the basis of the aforesaid determination, the petitioner- landowner filed execution applications, which were disposed of vide impugned order dated 07.07.2025.
Hence, the present revision petition(s).
CONTENTION(S):

ON BEHALF OF THE PETITOINER(S)-LANDOWNER(S) [8] The main grouse raised on behalf of the petitioner-landowner is that the execution application has been disposed off without even referring to the calculation sheet provided by her,
based on the determination made upto the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
It has, thus, been submitted that the impugned order is liable to be set aside.
ON BEHALF OF RESPONDENT(S)-STATE OF HARYANA

[9] On the other hand,
learned counsel for the respondents submits that the petitioner(s)-landowner(s) have already been released the entire amount of compensation as assessed upto the Hon'ble Apex Court, and, therefore, the impugned order calls for no interference.
[10] I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the paper-book.
3 of 4 CR No. 7621 of 2025 (O&M) and "21" connected cases 4

[11] A perusal of the impugned award dated 07.07.2025 passed by the learned Executing Court shows that no reference, at all, has been made therein to the calculations provided by the decree-holders, i.e., petitioner(s)- landowner(s).

Since the execution application(s) relate to release of amount of compensation, therefore, the learned Executing Court while disposing off these application(s), was required to at least consider Himani Alias Himani Grewal Toor vs State Of Haryana And Others on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118620454/
2 and record the details of the amount claimed by the decree-holder(s)/landowner(s) by comparing the same with the calculations provided by both the parties.

entities.text: Himani Alias Himani Grewal Toor vs State Of Haryana And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [12] In such circumstances, the impugned order dated 07.07.2025 passed by the learned Executing Court is unsustainable in the eyes of law being non-speaking/unreasoned.
[13] Consequently, the impugned order dated 07.07.2025 is hereby set aside.

The matter is remanded back to the learned Executing Court with request to decide with the matter afresh after taking into account the calculations provided by the petitioner(s)-landowner(s) in accordance with law.
[14] All the revision petition(s) stand disposed off accordingly.
[15] Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall stand(s) dis- posed off.
(HARKESH MANUJA)
JUDGE 02.12.2025 kv/d k kamra
Whether speaking/reasoned : Yes/No  Whether reportable : Yes/No
